subject: Lock + Burst Shield — renewal amendment proposal (EmberGrid)
messages:
From: Jaspreet Singh <jaspreet@embergrid.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: contracting@embergrid.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning + request for short price shelter and surge buffer

Hi Lauren,

Renewal for EmberGrid is coming up in mid-August and the exec team asked me to reach out earlier this cycle. We expect a larger-than-normal seasonal uplift driven by a product launch (see attached forecast).

Ask: can Redwood provide a short-term price shelter for 6-9 months at our current committed rate while we scale, and a complementary "surge buffer" (credits or softened overage) to cover unexpected spikes? Our risk is being rate-locked into a new higher price for a quarter where usage explodes while our revenue cadence lags.

A few constraints on our side: we can sign a modest amendment and update the PO quickly if terms are clear; procurement prefers a capped one-time credit rather than a permanent tier shift. Happy to jump on a call this week to walk through the numbers.

Attachments: embergrid-usage-forecast-q3-q4.xlsx

Thanks,
Jaspreet
Head of Platform Operations
EmberGrid

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jaspreet Singh <jaspreet@embergrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + request for short price shelter and surge buffer

Hi Jaspreet — thanks for the forecast and the heads-up. We can absolutely work with you to avoid a pricing shock during launch week. High-level proposal from our side (we can refine on a call):

- Contract lock: hold current per-token rate for 9 months (amendment) up to 1.5x your current annual committed units.
- Surge Shield: first 20% above the committed monthly run rate covered by a credit pool; overages between 20–50% billed at current rate with a 40% discount; anything above 50% billed at list.
- One-time launch credit: $40k in professional services/credits to help with onboarding and cache-warming.

If EmberGrid is comfortable with the 1.5x ceiling and the $40k one-time credit, we can draft a short amendment and routing PO. I copied Ben and Rishi to confirm commercial alignment, and Vanessa for the operational handoff.

Proposed next step: 30-minute alignment call tomorrow to finalize thresholds.

Attachment: redwood-proposed-amendment-draft.docx

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 12:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + request for short price shelter and surge buffer

Quick thoughts — I like the structure but suggest two small edits before we send to EmberGrid:

1) Make the surge buffer a % of monthly committed units rather than run-rate to keep measurement simple (e.g., 20% of monthly committed units).
2) Increase the one-time credit to $50k, but split it 50/50 between usage credits and PS to ensure they engage with our CS team during launch.

If Rishi signs off on the margin impact, I can push approval and prepare a clean amendment for signature.

—Ben
Account Executive

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + request for short price shelter and surge buffer

Ben + Lauren — approve the structure with a tweak. Finance is willing to accept a $50k one-time credit (split PS/usage) if EmberGrid commits to a minimum 12-month extension on the base contract term (we'd convert the lock into a 9-month price shelter but require an additional 12-month term to balance unit economics).

Grace — can you confirm that obligating an extra 12 months triggers any billing or revenue recognition issues? Also want a quick check on the legal template for the amendment.

If EmberGrid is comfortable with the extended term, we can finalize.

—Rishi
VP, Sales Operations

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jaspreet Singh <jaspreet@embergrid.com>
Cc: contracting@embergrid.com, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lock + Burst Shield — renewal amendment proposal (EmberGrid)

Hi Jaspreet — following internal alignment, here’s the firm proposal for EmberGrid to review: 

1) Price Shelter: hold current per-token rate for 9 months (starts on effective date of amendment).
2) Commit & Term: EmberGrid signs a 12-month extension to the base contract (new term), which allows Redwood to offer the shelter.
3) Surge Shield: first 20% above monthly committed units covered by a credit pool; overage between 20–50% billed at current rate with a 40% discount; >50% billed at list. Measurement will use monthly aggregated usage aligned to the committed unit definition in SOW.
4) One-time Launch Credit: $50,000 total — $25k applied as usage credits, $25k reserved for PS/enablement (redeemable within 90 days).

If that sounds acceptable, I’ll send the amendment for signature via DocuSign and we can have contracting email a PO. Next steps from our side: Vanessa will schedule a launch ops kick-off and Ben will move the DocuSign link once contracting confirms.

Link: https://www.docusign.com/link/eg-2026-42-amendment

Thanks and happy to hop on a quick call if you want to edit thresholds.

Best,
Lauren
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
